First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{7\pi }{24}$ into the above, we get

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{7\pi }{24})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12}).
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{24})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the double-angle formula once more with $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$, we can further simplify the above expression: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})} & =\frac{2\cdot 2}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{7\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})} \\  & =\frac{4}{(-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =-8\end{aligned}
$$
